source.title: Universal Redundancies in Time Series Foundation Models
source.authors: Anthony Bao; Venkata Hasith Vattikuti; Jeffrey Lai; William Gilpin

page_placements.theme: Induction-like copying in other modalities and non-autoregressive models

record.tranche_reason: The study applies a repeated-random-tokens test, following the original induction-head procedure, to a new model setting and measures prefix matching and copying.
record.gate_note: Appendix H reports induction-head measurements for Chronos. The study does not test induction-head formation during training, token-index loss changes, or few-shot task learning.
record.test_reason: The study applies the original repeated-random-tokens test to Chronos, a time-series encoder-decoder model. It finds heads that both prefix-match and copy, which bears on whether induction heads appear in a new modality and architecture (V4). It does not examine composition with previous-token heads, training dynamics, or in-context-learning loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find 8.3% of Chronos heads are RRT induction heads. Overlap with sharp heads is better than chance but limited: about 80% of sharp heads are not induction heads. Those non-induction sharp heads still copy context motifs, so TSFMs may perform induction through a different paradigm than the RRT test measures.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the repeated-random-tokens test and prefix-matching/copying criteria associated with the cited original procedure, adapted to Chronos's encoder-decoder setup and tokenizer; 32 sampled token IDs are repeated 4 times.
record.method_sensitivity: The classification of induction and sharp heads is sensitive to threshold choices; relaxing the sharp-head criterion changes the induction-head overlap estimate.

fits_no_version.finding: Only about 20% of low-entropy 'sharp' heads in Chronos meet the RRT induction criteria, a share stable across thresholds. Between 16.7% and 50-60% of induction heads are sharp, depending on thresholds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In time-series transformers, heads that match and copy context motifs are largely distinct from RRT-defined induction heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating diffuse heads preserves context parroting. Ablating one or a few sharp heads destroys forecast structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Context-motif parroting in Chronos depends on a small set of sharp cross-attention heads, mostly not RRT induction heads.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The induction-head test was run only on Chronos because it was the only model in the study with a uniform-binning tokenizer and without patches. Classification depends on chosen thresholds. The study does not test previous-token-head composition, training-time emergence, or in-context-learning loss changes.

untested.parts: Composition with an earlier previous-token head; the [A][B]…[A]→[B] circuit in small attention-only models. Chronos is not such a model and no composition analysis is done.
No token-index loss or in-context-learning attribution to induction heads.
Only Chronos is tested. The RRT test was not run on the patched TSFMs (Chronos-Bolt, Chronos 2, TimesFM, Toto, Moirai), and no other sizes or training runs were examined.
Not tested; the study measures no few-shot task learning.

missing.what: Dependence of the induction-head count on prefix, copy and entropy thresholds, swept in Figure 28F; no row records how the 8.3% figure changes.

record.verdict_notes: The study's main topic is redundancy and head ablation in time-series foundation models; induction heads appear only in Appendix H. The reader's V1 link is wrong because the subject is not a small attention-only model and composition is not tested, so r1 is relinked to V4. The study is not an original source. The test uses cross-attention from decoder to encoder, an adaptation of the RRT procedure.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures prefix matching and copying, but not composition with an earlier previous-token head; it tests Chronos, not a small attention-only transformer.
